To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
miRNAs are important regulators of leukotrienes and prostanoids, which are important mediators of inflammation and cancer.
miRNAs regulate eicosanoid formation and function and that miRNAs form complex regulatory networks that control eicosanoid biosynthesis and action.

miR-155 and miR-125b are key miRNAs that regulate leukotriene synthesis in human mast cells and that miR-21, miR-155, miR-146a, miR-27b, and miR-29a are key miRNPs that control the formation of prostaglandins in human monocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of new microRNA (miRNA) targets and the characterization of their biological functions, with a special focus on the regulation of eicosanoid biosynthesis and the development of novel therapeutical strategies.
the elucidation of molecular mechanisms that control leukotriene biosynthesis and function in human cells.
the elucidation of the role of miRNAs in the regulation of eicosanoid biosynthesis, with the goal of identifying novel therapeutic targets for inflammatory and neoplastic diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
miRNAs are important regulators of eicosanoid synthesis, which are involved in the control of inflammatory processes, cell growth and differentiation.
miRNAs are important regulators of eicosanoid synthesis and their dysregulation is associated with inflammatory and neoplastic diseases.
miRNAs play a major role in the regulation of the biosynthesis of eicosanoids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of several miRNAs is regulated by the availability of eicosanoids and that the expression of eicosanoid biosynthetic enzymes and their receptors is regulated by several miRNAs.

the regulation of leukotrienes by microRNAs is an important topic of research in the field of eicosanoid biology and has the potential to contribute to the development and application of novel therapeutic strategies in the treatment of inflammatory and allergic diseases.
miRNA regulation is a novel and important mechanism to fine-tune the production of eicosanoids.
The main takeaway from our work is that

miRNAs have the potential to regulate all major steps of eicosanoid biosynthesis, including the transcriptional regulation of biosynthetic enzymes, the post-transcriptional regulation of mRNA stability or translational control of enzymes, the regulation of eicosanoids themselves and the modulation of their biological effects.
miRNAs are not only involved in the regulation of single eicosanoid biosynthesis pathways but that they form complex regulatory circuits with other miRNAs.
miRNAs are important regulators of eicosanoid formation and their expression is often altered during disease progression.
